newsitem.title: INDIA: India seen world's largest palm oil consumer soon.
newsitem.headline: India seen world's largest palm oil consumer soon.

text.p: India is jostling with Pakistan and China for the top slot as the world's largest importer of palm oil, a Malaysian trade official said on Thursday.
Indian palm oil imports this year are projected to almost match China's, the chief executive officer of the Malaysian Palm Oil Promotion Council (MPOPC), Mohammed Hashim, told reporters.

Combined with the effect of India's higher population growth of 2.1 percent against China's one percent, Hashim said he believed this meant Indian palm oil imports would soon match or even exceed China's.

"India's per capita consumption of palm oil is 6.7 kgs against 10 kgs for China," Hashim said. "The World Health Organisation recommends oil consumption levels of around 20 to 24 kg per capita. So there is lot of opportunity to grow more."
Hashim was speaking ahead of a four-day-long promotion programme the MPOPC plans to begin in Bombay on Friday.

Though India ranks third among the world's producers of edible oil, it is unable to satisfy the needs of its 930-million-strong population. It has an estimated shortfall of about half-a-million tonnes, the MPOPC said.
"With the per capita consumption growing at about six percent per annum due to the increasing population and better purchasing power, this gap is guaranteed to widen," the MPOPC said in a statement.

Malaysia is the world's largest producer of palm oil, with an output of 7.8 million tonnes last year, Hashim said. This accounts for 52 percent of world production. India imports about 80 percent of its palm oil from Malaysia.
India imported 680,000 tonnes of palm oil upto August 31 this year, compared to the 750,000 tonnes the country imported in 1995, Hashim said.
"We are very optimistic that India will take at least one million tonnes this year," he said.
Pakistan imported 1.1 million tonnes of palm oil last year, with China importing around one million tonnes and India in third place with 750,000 tonnes.

Indian traders said earlier this week that they expected the country would import an additional 350,000 tonnes of palmolein in September and October. Palmolein is a refined, bleached deodorised form of palm oil.
"Imports of about 350,000 tonnes of palmolein are expected during September and October," G.K. Sood, chief executive of the Vanaspati Manufacturers' Association of India, had said.
